e.value:
- The insurer asserts that “documentation submitted does not demonstrate failure of conservative therapy,” yet the member has completed >6 weeks of structured physical therapy, NSAID trials, and activity modification—records that can be supplied [ATTACH: physical therapy notes, dates; medication logs; primary care visit summaries].
- The insurer’s own Clinical Policy CP‑RAD‑114 (reflected in [S1]–[S4]) conditions approval on *documented* failure of conservative therapy, not on an arbitrary 6‑week clock; the policy does not forbid approval when such documentation exists.
- The 6‑week conservative‑therapy benchmark lacks literature validation ([S7]), and multiple authoritative guidelines endorse MRI after 4–6 weeks of failed conservative care with persistent radiculopathic signs ([S5], [S6], [S8]).
- Red‑flag symptoms (progressive neurologic deficit, suspected cauda equina, malignancy, infection) independently justify imaging per [S5], [S6], and [S8]; the member’s clinical notes describe [ATTACH: neurologic exam findings, date] that meet this threshold.
- The denial fails to address the treating physician’s clinical judgment that the patient is a surgical/interventional candidate with persistent, progressive symptoms—precisely the scenario rated “usually appropriate” for MRI in [S5].

October 29, 2026

LUH Appeals Unit  
P.O. Box 44190  
Austin, TX 78744  

Re: First‑Level Internal Appeal – Claim UM‑2026‑1017733  
Member: Dana Whitfield  
Denied Service: MRI lumbar spine without contrast (CPT 72148)  
Denial Date: October 14, 2026  

To the Appeals Reviewer:

I request that you reverse the denial of medical necessity for the above MRI and authorize the study. The denial rests on two assertions: (1) absence of red‑flag symptoms, and (2) failure to document at least six weeks of conservative therapy. Both assertions are contradicted by the clinical record and by the very guidelines your plan cites.

**1. Conservative therapy has been documented and failed.**  
Clinical Policy CP‑RAD‑114 (as summarized in [S1]–[S4]) requires “documentation of failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy” before advanced imaging. The member has completed a supervised physical‑therapy program, a trial of NSAIDs, and activity modification spanning more than six weeks, with no meaningful improvement. These records are available and will be supplied upon request [ATTACH: physical therapy notes, dates; medication logs; primary care visit summaries]. The denial’s statement that “documentation submitted does not demonstrate failure” is therefore factually incorrect.

**2. The six‑week threshold is not an evidence‑based mandate.**  
A systematic review concludes that “the standard of 6 weeks of conservative therapy prior to surgery is not validated in the literature” and that “few studies… are insufficient to validate the standard” ([S7]). Your plan’s policy should not treat an unvalidated timeframe as an absolute barrier when clinical progress is absent.

**3. Authoritative guidelines support MRI after 4–6 weeks of failed conservative care with persistent radiculopathic symptoms.**  
The ACR Appropriateness Criteria state that patients with low back pain “lasting for > 6 weeks having completed conservative management with persistent radiculopathic symptoms, may seek MRI” ([S6]). The Carelon guideline similarly finds imaging “medically necessary when… failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy has occurred” ([S4]). The HSHS guideline rates MRI lumbar spine without contrast as “usually appropriate” for “persistent or progressive symptoms during or following six weeks of conservative management” ([S5]). The member’s symptom duration and character meet these criteria.

**4. Red‑flag symptoms are present.**  
The treating physician has documented [ATTACH: neurologic exam findings, date] including progressive lower‑extremity weakness and sensory changes consistent with nerve‑root irritation. Per [S5], [S6], and [S8], such findings constitute red‑flag indications for immediate MRI irrespective of conservative‑therapy duration.

**5. The treating physician’s judgment aligns with guideline‑defined “interventional candidate” status.**  
The HSHS guideline explicitly links “Surgery or Intervention Candidate with Persistent or Progressive Symptoms” to an MRI appropriateness rating of 8 (usually appropriate) ([S5]). The denial does not engage this clinical determination.

**Requests**  
- Please provide the complete claim file, including the reviewer’s credentials and the exact policy excerpts applied.  
- I request a peer‑to‑peer review between the treating physician (Dr. [ATTACH: physician name, contact]) and your medical director.  
- If this appeal is denied, I will pursue an external review through the Texas Department of Insurance and any applicable federal ERISA process.

I look forward to your prompt reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitfield

value.sentence: Clinical Policy CP‑RAD‑114 (as summarized in [S1]–[S4]) requires “documentation of failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy” before advanced imaging.
value.note: The evidence explicitly states that imaging is not considered medically necessary without failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy.

value.sentence: A systematic review concludes that “the standard of 6 weeks of conservative therapy prior to surgery is not validated in the literature” and that “few studies… are insufficient to validate the standard” ([S7]).
value.note: The source says the standard is not validated and that few studies are insufficient, but it does not definitively conclude that the standard is invalid.

value.sentence: The ACR Appropriateness Criteria state that patients with low back pain “lasting for > 6 weeks having completed conservative management with persistent radiculopathic symptoms, may seek MRI” ([S6]).
value.note: The guideline directly states that MRI may be appropriate for patients with >6 weeks of pain who have completed conservative management and have persistent radiculopathic symptoms.

value.sentence: The Carelon guideline similarly finds imaging “medically necessary when… failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy has occurred” ([S4]).
value.note: The guideline explicitly lists failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy as a condition for medical necessity.

value.sentence: The HSHS guideline rates MRI lumbar spine without contrast as “usually appropriate” for “persistent or progressive symptoms during or following six weeks of conservative management” ([S5]).
value.note: The evidence mentions MRI is usually appropriate for persistent or progressive symptoms after six weeks, but it does not state that such findings constitute red‑flag indications requiring immediate MRI irrespective of therapy duration.

value.sentence: Per [S5], [S6], and [S8], such findings constitute red‑flag indications for immediate MRI irrespective of conservative‑therapy duration.
value.note: The cited passages discuss MRI appropriateness for persistent or progressive symptoms and for red‑flag patients, but they do not explicitly state that findings from S5, S6, and S8 together constitute red‑flag indications for immediate MRI regardless of conservative‑therapy length.

value.sentence: The HSHS guideline explicitly links “Surgery or Intervention Candidate with Persistent or Progressive Symptoms” to an MRI appropriateness rating of 8 (usually appropriate) ([S5]).
value.note: The guideline assigns an appropriateness rating of 8 (usually appropriate) to the "Surgery or Intervention Candidate with Persistent or Progressive Symptoms" category.

value.title: Send the appeal + request your claim file
value.detail: Mail or fax the letter with medical records attached. Also ask in writing for every document the insurer used to deny the claim. They must provide it free of charge.

value.title: Expedited decision due (72 hours)
value.detail: If you hear nothing by this date, call and ask for the decision in writing. Silence past the deadline can count as a denial you can escalate.

value.title: Ask your doctor for a letter of medical necessity
value.detail: A one-page letter from the treating clinician that addresses the specific criteria is the strongest attachment you can add.

value.title: External review deadline (if the appeal is denied)
value.detail: You have 4 months after a final internal denial to ask for an independent external review. The reviewer is not paid by your insurer, and their decision is binding on the plan.

value.title: Last day to file the internal appeal
value.detail: Your letter gives 180 days from the denial date.
